# windows_installed_software (Data Source)

Reads the installed software inventory of the remote Windows host without managing it. This is a **standalone collection** data source — no sibling resource exists.

Inventory comes from the machine-wide Uninstall registry hives (the same hives `windows_legacy_package` reads), plus the loaded per-user hives under `HKU` when `include_user_installs` is set. Optional filters narrow the result: `name_regex` and `publisher_regex` (RE2 matches on the DisplayName and Publisher), `product_code` (an MSI ProductCode GUID in any common spelling), `include_system_components` (keep entries with `SystemComponent=1`, hidden from Programs and Features), `include_updates` (keep update entries) and `include_user_installs`. Omitted filters match everything.

`packages` carries one object per matching entry, sorted by name (case-insensitive), then version, then registry key; an empty match is a valid empty list, never an error. `skipped_entries` counts registry keys skipped because their values were unreadable (keys without a DisplayName are silently omitted and not counted). `Win32_Product` is never queried.

The Terraform data source ID is a query-ID: the hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Full installed-software inventory of the target host.
data "windows_installed_software" "all" {
  # No filters: full inventory.
}

# Only the .NET runtimes (updates and system components included).
data "windows_installed_software" "dotnet" {
  name_regex                = "Microsoft .NET.*"
  include_updates           = true
  include_system_components = true
}

output "installed_software_names" {
  value       = [for p in data.windows_installed_software.all.packages : p.name]
  description = "Display names of every installed package on the host."
}

output "dotnet_inventory" {
  value = [
    for p in data.windows_installed_software.dotnet.packages : {
      name         = p.name
      version      = p.version
      product_code = p.product_code
      scope        = p.scope
    }
  ]
  description = "Installed .NET packages with their versions and product codes."
}

output "skipped_entries" {
  value       = data.windows_installed_software.all.skipped_entries
  description = "Registry keys skipped because their values were unreadable."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_system_components` (Boolean) Keep entries with SystemComponent=1 (hidden from Programs and Features). Omit (null) means false.
- `include_updates` (Boolean) Keep update entries (ReleaseType of Security Update/Update/Hotfix, or a non-empty ParentKeyName). Omit (null) means false.
- `include_user_installs` (Boolean) Additionally enumerate the Uninstall hives of the loaded per-user hives under HKU (domain SIDs S-1-5-21-*); service SIDs excluded; unloaded profiles not scanned. Omit (null) means false.
- `name_regex` (String) Restrict the result to packages whose DisplayName matches this RE2 regular expression.
- `product_code` (String) Restrict the result to the package with this MSI ProductCode GUID, in any common spelling (with or without braces, any case).
- `publisher_regex` (String) Restrict the result to packages whose Publisher matches this RE2 regular expression.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source ID (query-ID); hex SHA-256 of the normalised filter set (regexes, normalised product code, bools).
- `packages` (Attributes List) Matching installed packages, sorted by name, version and registry key. Empty when no package matches the filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--packages))
- `skipped_entries` (Number) Number of registry keys skipped because their values were unreadable.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--packages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `packages`

Read-Only:

- `architecture` (String) Registry view the entry was read from: x86 for the WOW6432Node hive, otherwise the host architecture (x64 or arm64).
- `estimated_size_kb` (Number) EstimatedSize value in KB; 0 when unreported.
- `install_date` (String) Registry InstallDate normalised to YYYY-MM-DD; empty when the host value is missing or unparseable.
- `install_location` (String) InstallLocation, as observed on the host.
- `is_msi` (Boolean) True when the entry's WindowsInstaller value is 1.
- `name` (String) Package DisplayName, as observed on the host.
- `product_code` (String) MSI ProductCode GUID in upper-case with braces, derived from the registry key name; empty for non-MSI entries.
- `publisher` (String) Package publisher, as observed on the host.
- `quiet_uninstall_string` (String) QuietUninstallString, as observed on the host.
- `registry_key` (String) Full registry path of the entry.
- `scope` (String) machine for the HKLM hives, user for per-user HKU entries.
- `uninstall_string` (String) UninstallString, as observed on the host.
- `user_sid` (String) Owning user SID for user-scope entries; empty otherwise.
- `version` (String) DisplayVersion, as observed on the host.
